extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and applicants (Korea); patent attorneys interacting with KIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Official KIPO examination guidance on priority claims, domestic priority, disclosure exceptions, divisional/converted applications, legitimate-right-holder applications, and treatment of international (PCT) applications. Specifies deadlines, retroactivity rules, examiner actions, and evidentiary/translation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim not affected by fate of first application
rubrics_metrics.description: Even applications invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned or rejected after the filing can serve as a basis of claiming a right of priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner shall not examine whether the application in the first country which forms a basis of the priority claim is pending. The fate (invalidated/withdrawn/abandoned/rejected) of the first application does not by itself prevent claiming priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identical invention treated as filed on first-country filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention described in an application claiming a priority under the treaty is identical with the invention described in the application filed in the first country, the invention in the application claiming priority shall be treated as if filed on the filing date of the application in the first country for applying provisions in Articles 29, 36 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule is applied when determining the reference date for novelty/inventive step; reference date determination is generally done on a claim-by-claim basis (see related criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date determined claim-by-claim (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date for determining patentability shall be determined on a claim-by-claim basis in principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details follow depending on whether a claim is identical to a first-country disclosure, not described in the first-country application, or involves multiple priority claims. Examiner must apply rules per-claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date for claims identical to first-country application
rubrics_metrics.description: For an invention identical (including substantially/’de facto’ identical) to the invention of the application filed in the first country, the reference date shall be the filing date of the application in the first country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple priority claims (claims relying on two or more first-country applications), the reference date for the invention commonly described in multiple first-country applications shall be the earliest filing date among them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date for claims not described in first-country application
rubrics_metrics.description: For an invention which is not described in an application filed in the first country, the filing date of the application claiming priority under the treaty shall be the reference date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an invention is obtained by combining technical matters separately included in two or more first-country applications, or by combining matters from the first-country applications with new matter, it is treated as an invention not described in the first-country application (and thus the later filing date applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claims where the first-country application itself claims priority
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application filed in the first country claims the priority right based on another earlier application, the application shall not be regarded as the 'earliest application' prescribed in Article 4 C(2) of the Paris Convention for the invention described in both the application and the earlier application; the effect of the priority claim shall not be recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination shall not be conducted retroactively to the reference date in such cases, and the examiner shall notify a specific reason for non-retroactive application. If prior art discovered prevents retroactivity between earliest date and filing date of the priority claim, the examiner must state the reason for non-retroactive application in the notice of grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for submission of evidential documents for priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidential documents for the priority claim shall be submitted within one year and four months from the earliest filing date; failure to submit within the statutory period causes the priority claim to lose its effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner discovers evidential documents are not submitted, a procedural amendment is requested and the priority claim is invalidated if the deficiency is not amended. Submission after the statutory period cannot cure the procedural deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption via DAS / online exchange for evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a copy of the description or drawings of the invention of the application filed in the first country can be exempted if the application is filed in countries equipped with an online system for exchange of evidential documents (Direct-attached Storage, DAS) and agree for on-line delivery (e.g., Japan, EPO, US, WIPO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where eligible, on-line exchange replaces physical submission of those evidential documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of application number may substitute for document submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The indication of the application number whose priority is claimed in the application may substitute for the submission of documents stating the application number of the application filed in the first country in accordance with Article 54(4)(ii) of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This substitution can fulfill the procedural requirement for evidential documents in applicable cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may request translations of priority evidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If considered necessary (e.g., there exists prior art during the period between the priority date and the filing date), the examiner may set a time period and request submission of translations of evidential documents for the priority claim into Korean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claimant fails to submit translations within the prescribed period, the examiner may invalidate the priority claim procedure. Use of translations depends on examiner’s discretion when prior art issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority: applicant eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A person eligible to claim domestic priority is an applicant of the prior-filed application. If the applicant of the prior-filed application and the applicant of the later-filed application are not the same, the examiner shall request amendments and invalidate the priority claim procedure if the deficiency is not cured. The scope of amendments is limited to correction of obvious errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether applicants are the same is determined as of when the domestic priority claim has been filed (cover sheet or amendment time). Examiner must enforce identity of applicants at claim filing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority: one-year filing period
rubrics_metrics.description: The domestic priority claim shall be made within one year from the filing date of the prior-filed application which forms the basis of the domestic priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed after the statutory period, the examiner requests amendments and invalidates the priority claim procedure if deficiency is not cured; scope of amendment limited to obvious errors and this is stated in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional or converted applications cannot be basis of domestic priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisional or converted applications shall not serve as a basis of domestic priority claim. Where domestic priority is based on such applications, the examiner requests amendments and invalidates the priority claim procedure if the deficiency is not cured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the basis application for domestic priority is an original prior-filed application, not a divisional/converted filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed applications that are invalidated/withdrawn/etc cannot serve as basis for domestic priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application has been invalidated, withdrawn, or abandoned or where the decision to grant a patent or utility model registration or to reject the application has become conclusive and binding, the application cannot serve as a basis of a claim of domestic priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior-filed application falls under these cases, the examiner requests amendments and invalidates the priority claim procedure if not cured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority: identical-invention retroactivity and claim-by-claim rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Where inventions claimed in the later application and those stated in the original specification/drawings of the prior-filed application are identical (including 'de facto identical'), the later application shall be deemed to have been filed at the time of the prior-filed application for applying Articles 29, 36 etc.; effects are determined on a claim-by-claim basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple domestic priority claims, when the invention is stated in two or more original specifications of prior-filed applications, the reference date is the earliest filing date. If the claimed invention is not stated in the original specification of the prior-filed application, the filing date of the domestic priority claim is the reference date; combinations of matters from multiple prior-filed applications or with new matter are treated as not stated in the prior-filed original specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: When prior-filed application itself claims priority, priority effect not recognized for overlapping inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the prior-filed application which forms the basis of the domestic priority claim itself claims priority based on another earlier application, the effect of the domestic priority claim shall not be recognized for inventions stated in both the prior-filed application and the other priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination shall not be carried out retroactively to the earlier reference date; examiner must specify the reason for non-retroactive application in the notice of grounds for rejection if prior art prevents retroactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application deemed withdrawn after one year three months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the inventions stated in the original specification/drawings of the later application and those in the original specification of the prior-filed application are identical, the prior-filed application, which shall be deemed to have been withdrawn when one year and three months has lapsed from the filing date, is regarded to be laid open at the time when the application with the priority claim is laid open or published in the patent gazette for purposes of Article 29(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the examiner discovers an application under examination has become a basis for a domestic priority claim, he/she shall defer further examination. If the domestic priority claim is invalidated due to formal deficiency, the examiner shall resume examination on the suspended application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to grant patent on domestic priority deferred until prior-filed application withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to grant a patent on the domestic priority claim shall be deferred until the prior-filed application is considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When examiner carries out expedited examination on the application with the domestic priority claim, he/she shall notify the applicant that the decision to grant a patent will be deferred until the prior-filed application is withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure exception: filing deadline relative to publication date
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application claiming disclosure exceptions under Article 30(2) is filed, the examiner shall examine whether the application is filed within twelve months (six months for applications filed before March 14, 2012) from the prescribed publication date stated in the application. If filed after the statutory period, request amendments and invalidate the claim if deficiency not cured; untimely claim is not overcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict statutory time limits apply; examiner must check the relevant publication date and applicable transitional six-month rule for pre-2012 filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure exception where publication was by person entitled to patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where disclosure exception is claimed because the publication was made by a person with an entitlement to obtain a patent, the examiner shall examine whether (a) the person is entitled to obtain a patent upon the public disclosure, (b) the claim is made in the application, and (c) the evidential document of the public disclosure is submitted within thirty days from the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deficiencies are found, request amendments and invalidate the claim if not cured. Pay special attention where the discloser and applicant differ, where type/date of disclosure are incorrect, evidential documents do not sufficiently specify the invention, or evidential documents are submitted without stating the purport for the disclosure-exception claim (when submitted on filing date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple public disclosures and inseparable relations
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiple public disclosures, where the purport of disclosure exceptions is indicated and evidential documents for each disclosure are submitted, disclosure exceptions shall be applied to each disclosure. However, for disclosures in inseparable relation, evidential documents for the initial disclosure suffice and subsequent documents need not be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: exhibition displays and separate market sales generally require documents for both, but if market sales are closely connected to the exhibition by contract, submission for market sales can be exempt. Each claim for disclosure exception is judged individually. If a disclosure exception is recognized as legitimate, novelty and inventive step are judged as if the concerned invention were not publicly known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a divisional or converted application; identity of applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who can file a divisional or converted application is an applicant of the original application. Where applicants are not identical (all applicants must be same if several), an examiner shall provide an opportunity for petition and then return the application to an applicant. Scope of amendments for correcting applicants limited to obvious errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether applicants are the same is assessed as of the time when the divisional or converted application is submitted; legitimate changes in applicant name on the filing date are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for filing divisional and converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application shall be filed only during the period designated for amendment of specification/drawings or within three months from the date a certified copy of the decision to grant a patent or the trial decision revoking the decision to reject is served (but not after patent registration), or within the period designated for appeal against decision to reject. A converted application shall be filed within thirty days from the date that an applicant initially receives a certified copy of the decision to reject (or extended period if extension approved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an appeal is filed, a divisional may be filed within thirty days from transmittal of the certified copy of decision to reject (or extended Article 132(3) period). Where filed after statutory period, examiner provides opportunity for petition and then returns application pursuant to Article 11 of Enforcement Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional/converted applications cannot be based on invalidated/terminated originals
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an original application has been invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or where the decision to reject has become conclusive and binding, division or conversion shall not be made based on the application. Converted applications cannot be filed after registration of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If original falls under these cases, examiner provides opportunity for petition then returns the application. If divisional/converted was filed legitimately before original procedure terminated, the divisional is regarded as valid and examination begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of divisional matters must be within original disclosure; treatment of scope violations (pre- and post-2006)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters described in specification or drawings of divisional applications must be within scope of matters described in original specification/drawings. Where division/conversion is outside scope, treatment depends on filing date of original application: (i) original filed before Sept 30, 2006: deliver preliminary notice for inadmissible division(conversion), allow statement; if not cured, deliver notice for inadmissible division and conduct examination as of filing date of divisional (not retroactively). If cured during exam, exam is retroactive to original filing date; (ii) original filed after Oct 1, 2006: deliver written notice of ground for rejection for scope violation and, if not cured, decide to reject. If other grounds for rejection exist, include them in same written notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where application contains both inadmissible division reason and ground for rejection, confirm admissibility before notifying rejection ground; examiner may nonetheless deliver preliminary notice and ground for rejection simultaneously where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a divisional claims same invention as original after division (Article 36(2) issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a divisional is made legally and a claimed invention of the divisional is identical to a claimed invention of the original application after the division, the applications shall be subject to Article 36(2). Amendments of the original application are required and shall be made at the time of filing date of the divisional application (Enforcement Rules Article 29(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper amendment timing to avoid double-patenting/conflict between parent and divisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-level divisional/converted applications can inherit original filing date if requirements met
rubrics_metrics.description: If Application A is divided into B and B is divided into C, Application C is regarded legitimate and deemed filed at time of Application A provided (a) B met all requirements for division as to A, and (b) C met all requirements for division as to B, and (c) invention of C is within scope of original disclosure of A. A converted application is treated likewise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactivity of filing date for multi-level divisions depends on each intermediate divisional having met substantive/formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by a legitimate right holder: statutory requirements (four conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be recognized as an application by a legitimate right holder (Articles 34 and 35), the following must be met: (1) an application by the unentitled person was filed earlier than the application of the legitimate holder; (2) the unentitled person's application is rejected or invalidated in a trial on the ground it was not filed by the entitled person; (3) the application by the legitimate holder is filed within thirty days from the date when the trial decision became conclusive and unappealable; and (4) the scope of the claimed invention in the legitimate holder's application falls within the scope of disclosure of the unentitled person's application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where legitimate-holder filing uses Form (xiv) or arguments during examination, the examiner shall assess legitimacy before other rejection grounds. If examiner doubts conditions (1),(3),(4), deliver notice that filing date shall not be retroactive. If condition (2) not satisfied, examination is deferred until the trial decision is final and conclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and scope when application by legitimate right holder is recognized
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is recognized as legitimate, it is deemed to have been filed at the date when the unentitled person filed. Judgments of patent requirements, period calculations, and related provisions shall be determined as of the unentitled person's filing date. Scope of invention is limited to claimed inventions and those disclosed in the unentitled person's specification/drawings; inventions beyond that scope are not retroactive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a third-party application filed between the unentitled person's filing and the legitimate holder's filing shall not cause rejection of the legitimate holder's application because the legitimate holder's filing date is retroactive to the unentitled person's earlier filing. Requests for examination filed after three years from the unentitled person's filing date are valid if filed simultaneously with the legitimate-holder’s application.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) application treatment and Korean translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An international patent application (PCT) where the filing date is established under the PCT and Korea is designated is treated as a regular patent application filed on the international filing date except for certain exceptional clauses (including enlarged concept of novelty). An international application filed in a foreign language is deemed withdrawn if its Korean translation is not submitted per Article 201 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects arising from submission of a translation differ depending on filing date (special rules for applications filed before Dec 31, 2014 vs after Jan 1, 2015) regarding which parts (description, claims, drawings, abstract) are considered originally filed in Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions and priority treatment for international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When an international application enters the national phase with Korean translation submitted and claims priority under the PCT, the priority claim is treated as the treaty priority. If the application serving as basis is a Korean application or an international application where Korea is the only designated State, the priority claim is considered domestic. If an international application serves as basis of domestic priority and becomes 'another application' under Article 29(3), it is considered laid open at the time of international publication; scope limited to inventions described as of international filing date and its translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person claiming disclosure exceptions for an invention claimed in an international application may submit a written statement and evidential documents within 30 days from the reference date even if the purport was not stated in the international application. Korean translations of PCT Article 19/34 amendments submitted within reference date are treated as voluntary amendments under Article 47. Examiner may request copies of documents cited in the ISR/IPER; Commissioner may request submission within a designated period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special provisions for enlarged concept of novelty for international applications (date-dependent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special provisions regarding the enlarged concept of novelty apply depending on filing dates of the concerned and 'another application'. For example: (i) where both applications were filed before Dec 31, 2014 (or 'another application' before Dec 31, 2014 but concerned later), an international application relied upon as 'another application' is considered laid open at international publication but scope limited to inventions described in specification/claims/drawings as of the international filing date and its translation; (ii) where both filed after Jan 1, 2015, scope of 'another application' is limited to inventions described in the description/claims/drawings as filed. International applications deemed withdrawn for failure to submit Korean translation per Article 201(4) cannot be 'another application' for enlarged concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply transitional/temporal rules carefully to decide scope of prior international applications when judging novelty under expanded concept rules.
